title: IMPACT score pour Outcomes dans Head lésion
formula:
Probability of 6-month mortality or unfavorable outcome = 1 / (1 + e^-x^), where x is as follows:

| Model | 6-month outcome | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mortality | Unfavorable outcome* | |
| Core | x = -3.109 + addition of the selected points** | x = -2.644 + addition of the selected points |
| Extended | x = -3.787 + addition of the selected points | x = -3.023 + addition of the selected points |
| Lab | x = -3.184 + addition of the selected points | x = -2.470 + addition of the selected points |

*Unfavorable outcome = death, persistent vegetative state, or severe disability.

**Points for each variable in the core, extended, and lab models are provided below.

how_to_use.why: Prognostic models aim to provide a spectrum of probable outcomes in patients based on populations of patients. This tool provides useful information that may help clinicians and surrogate decisionmakers to determine the goals of treatment and care relative to the possibilities of outcomes.
how_to_use.when: Patients ≥14 years old admitted to critical care units with [GCS](nabda:calc.glasgow-coma-scale-score-gcs) ≤12 (moderate and severe TBI).
how_to_use.pearls:
- Developed to provide early prognostication; therefore, data from the first 24 hours of admission should be used.
- Should NOT be used for serial evaluations or updating prognosis with progression of care.
- Original datasets were developed in high-income countries and therefore may not be applicable in developing countries or areas with otherwise limited medical resources.
- Best used for isolated head injuries, as other comorbidities and extracranial injuries are not taken into consideration in this score and may contribute to patient mortality.

next_steps.critical_actions: Outcomes are meant to describe prognosis on the population level. It should NOT be used as alone for clinical decisionmaking in individual patients such as withholding aggressive therapies.

evidence:
The International Mission for Prognosis and Analysis of Clinical Trials in TBI (IMPACT) project was a collaborative effort to standardize research practices in the study of TBI. The IMPACT database, consisting of patient data from eight randomized controlled trials and three observational studies between 1984 and 1997, is the source from which the models presented here were developed ([Steyerberg 2008](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC2494563/pdf/pmed.0050165.pdf)).

Using 8,509 patients age 14 and up with moderate to severe TBI, the IMPACT investigators developed three models based on variables previously described to have prognostic value ([Murray 2007](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/17375997)). Each subsequent model builds on the previous to add additional clinical data when available.

Primary outcomes for prediction were 6-month mortality and 6-month outcomes dichotomized as favorable (Glasgow Outcome Score (GOS) 4-5) and unfavorable (GOS 1-3).

The models were internally validated using data sets within the IMPACT database, then externally validated with patients from the Medical Research Council Corticosteroid Randomization of Significant Head Injury (MRC CRASH) trial, which included 6,681 eligible patients.
